expectations.text: Time and the janitor run under testing/synctest; any time.Sleep sits inside a bubble; no polling loops
expectations.evidence: Both tests run under synctest.Test (lines 58, 150) and their four sleeps (lines 87, 98, 101, 114) sit inside the TestExpiryLifecycle bubble, and grep shows no polling loops (the only `for` statements are `for i := range 8` fan-out and the panic case table). But Example_sessionTokens contains `time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)` at line 37 OUTSIDE any bubble: the example demonstrates TTL expiry by really sleeping past a 50ms deadline. The sleep is deterministic (expiry is enforced on read via monotonic time.Now comparison, and Sleep guarantees at least its duration), so it cannot flake, but the assertion's literal clause 'any time.Sleep sits inside a bubble' is violated; the expiry story was already covered inside a bubble by TestExpiryLifecycle, so the example did not need real time to pass.
